Automate Freight Accounting and Trigger Invoicing from Delivery Evidence

Thematic Area: Freight Finance Automation & Connected Accounting

How might we automate freight accounting and use accepted proof of delivery to trigger accurate customer invoicing in the ERP?

Background

A shipping and logistics group wants to automate more of its freight-forwarding finance operations. It requires AI-powered accounting capabilities and a connection between proof of delivery (POD), validated shipment charges and ERP invoice issuance.

The objective is to reduce repeated data entry, improve accounting consistency and shorten the handover from completed delivery to customer billing. Accepted POD and satisfaction of agreed billing conditions should trigger the corresponding ERP invoice through the defined approval process.

Relevant startups offer accounting automation, document processing, delivery-management software and enterprise-system integration.

Significance of Problem

Key challenges include:

  • Slower billing: Manual delivery checks and invoice preparation lengthen the delivery-to-billing cycle.
  • Accounting errors: Repeated entry and disconnected records create opportunities for incorrect charges and inconsistent financial information.
  • Higher administrative costs: Reconciling delivery evidence, invoices and accounting records consumes finance-team capacity.

Existing Efforts

  • Available capabilities: A supplier-invoice provider automates document capture, matching and reconciliation. A delivery-management provider supplies electronic POD and delivery records. An enterprise integration provider offers document extraction, approval workflows and connections to accounting or ERP systems.
  • Collaboration focus: Combine supplier-invoice automation with the wider accounting workflow. Connect accepted POD and validated shipment charges to ERP customer invoicing, define approvals and accounting rules, and test the complete delivery-to-billing process with the group’s systems.

Potential Market Size

  • Global accounting software and services market: The global market was estimated at US$20.8 billion in 2025 and is forecast to reach US$38.7 billion by 2033, with 8.1% annual growth during 2026–2033. Asia Pacific is forecast to grow fastest.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
